MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 5, 2015

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Schlicht at 5:00 p.m., on January 5, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on December 19, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel-Existing Litigation Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d)
  of Section 54956.9 Intervention into General Rate Case filed by SDG&E regarding
  the tariff upon utility owned street lights.

City Council Minutes  1  January 5, 2015
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Schlicht recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council addressed a general rate case where the City
is interacting with SDG&E. The Council will discuss the matter further under agenda item
18. The City Council gave direction to staff but no reportable action occurred in Closed Session.

Addition of a Late Arising Item Relating to Replacement of Two Heaters for the 50 Meter
Pool at the Marguerite Aquatics Complex (to be addressed under Staff Reports)

Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to declare that the need
to address the item rose subsequent to the posting of the agenda and that there is the need to take
immediate action (the matter will be heard under Staff Reports later in the meeting.)

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Opening Remarks from Mayor Schlicht

  Mayor Schlicht presented her opening remarks.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Bucknum

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Raths

  Mayor Schlicht and Community Services Supervisor Ashley Blair presented awards to Nila

City Council Minutes  2  January 5, 2015
 P3. Recognize Mission Viejo High School Varsity Football Team as CIF-Southern Section

P4. Recognize Trabuco Hills High School Varsity Football Team as CIF-Southern Section

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Sharon Cody, M.V.: discussed a flier that was mailed to residents from October 2014 until the
election on November 4. There was no disclaimer stating who distributed the mailer and she feels
that it was a Political Action Committee that failed to file any campaign finance forms. Mrs. Cody
noted that she has reported this to the FPPC enforcement division and she looks forward to their
determination.

David Anderson, Saddleback College, M.V.: congratulated the new City Council Members and
thanked those who voted to provide community grants for 2015, one of which was provided
to Saddleback College in conjunction with the Angels for the Arts. Mr. Anderson thanked the
Council and expressed the college's willingness to grow its partnership with the City.

Ryan R. Farsai, ARCO station owner, M.V.: discussed varying gasoline prices and the difficulty
he will have keeping his gas station open with the current competition between franchises.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 12 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

18.  Update on CPUC Consideration of SDG&E General Rate Case Matter

  City Attorney Curley announced that the administrative law judge found that the City of
  Mission Viejo does have standing and should be a party to the lawsuit. He noted that the
  City does audit utility costs and when staff finds opportunities to pursue rate reductions,
  they do pursue them.

19.  Use of Facilitator for January 16, 2015 Pre-Budget Discussion Meeting

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she wanted this item on the agenda to make the
  Council aware that the budget workshop would be a facilitator-run meeting.

20.  Urgency Ordinance Repealing Sections 2.06.050, 2.06.070 and 2.04.060 of the
  Mission Viejo Municipal Code and Adopting Revised Sections Regulating the
  Appointment and Removal of City Councilmember Appointees and Adopting
  Revised Sections to Replace Said Sections

  City Attorney Curley presented the staff report.

  Bruce Teel, M.V.: discussed the email he sent the Council earlier in the day and he
  outlined the reasons he strongly opposes this proposed ordinance.

  Mayor Schlicht expressed her desire for the commission appointment process to be
  changed and she stated that she likes Council Member Sachs' proposed improvements.
  The Council discussed the merits and downsides to changing the City's commission
  appointment process.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to table this
  matter indefinitely.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury

23.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum noted that she made some corrections to her AB1234 report and
removed two events that she was not able to attend. She outlined her attendance at recent events
including the tree lighting at Mission Hospital, the City's Animal Services volunteer holiday party,
the ACC-OC newly elected official’s policy briefing, the City employee's holiday luncheon, Diane
Harkey’s State Board of Equalization swearing-in ceremony, the Chamber of Commerce holiday
mixer, the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center holiday luncheon and the City’s
Santa's arrival celebration.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs stated that he too amended his AB1234 report to indicate that he was only
able to attend one event, the ACC-OC meeting for newly elected officials, which he found very
City Council Minutes  13  January 5, 2015
 informative. Noting a late fee on one of the check registers, Council Member Sachs stated that the
City should never have a late fee. He also pointed out that there were 15 police ambush deaths
last year as compared to 5 the previous year. Mr. Sachs stated that this is a horrible condition to
be living in and he is proud to say that he backs all first responders and if it were not for them,
we’d be having a lot of problems.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury announced that he had nothing to report this evening.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths thanked the people of Mission Viejo for a wonderful month of December
and he outlined his attendance at recent events including the grand re-opening of the food court at
the Shops at Mission Viejo, a ribbon cutting ceremony at a Christmas tree lot, the Mission Hospital
tree lighting celebration, the City of Newport Beach Council Member swearing-in ceremony, an
elected officials briefing and ethics training at ACC-OC, and an open house with Orange County
Supervisors Bartlett and Spitzer. He also attended holiday events for the City of Mission Viejo
staff, the Chamber of Commerce, the American Legion and an Eagle Scout ceremony with Troop
332. Mayor Pro Tem Raths outlined his visit with Lt. NewMyer and he noted that he is looking
forward to doing some ride-alongs with the deputies. He also discussed his tour of one of the fire
stations and he invited residents to contact him if they need a city official to attend an event.

Mayor Schlicht

Mayor Schlicht thanked her colleagues for their patience as she adjusts to the role of Mayor.
Referring to the presentations at the beginning of the meeting, she stated that she is so proud of
the artists and athletes who were honored. Mayor Schlicht noted that she had great fun watching
the football games this season and student athletes and artists do us proud. Following up on Council
Member Sachs’ comments, she said that it is unbelievable what is going on in our country right
now against our police. Mayor Schlicht stated that we are a nation of laws but are losing that slowly
and she concluded with a John Adams quote: “They define a republic to be a government of laws
and not of men.”

ADJOURNMENT
